subject: Uptime validation, SLO measurement, and read-only metrics access
messages:
From: Peter Liu <peter.liu@everleafhealth.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Procurement] Clarifying SLO measurement and dashboard access (Everleaf)

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Procurement and our platform reliability team are working through the final checklist before we sign the Dedicated reservation. Two quick asks so we can close: 

1) How do you measure availability for the SLA? Is uptime derived from a synthetic probe, customer-observed success rate, or both? What aggregation window (1 min / 5 min / 1 hr / 24 hr) do you use for calculating % uptime?

2) For latency commitments, we need the p95 and p99 measurement definitions (rolling window, sample population — e.g., successful generation requests only, or all requests including errors).

3) Who will have access to the metrics? We prefer a read-only dashboard for Everleaf engineers plus PagerDuty alerts for our on-call. Can read-only access be scoped to service/key level?

4) If Redwood requests an exception (e.g., for planned maintenance longer than the exception window), what is the approval flow and how are customers notified? Any credits or remediation tied to exceptions?

If you can respond to the four items and share any short spec or evidence (scraped logs, metric retention), I can run this by our legal and security procurement teams. Ideally before Thurs 11/12.

Thanks,
Peter Liu
Platform Architect, Everleaf Health

--
Everleaf Health | production@everleafhealth.com

From: ava.chen@redwood.ai
To: Peter Liu <peter.liu@everleafhealth.com>, procurement@everleafhealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Procurement] Clarifying SLO measurement and dashboard access (Everleaf)

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front; details and attachments below.

1) Availability (SLA):
- Primary signal: internal synthetic probes from multiple regions -> these run every 30s and exercise a representative generation path (auth -> small payload -> full response).
- Secondary signal: customer-observed success rate derived from production request logs (success = 2xx with no server-side error).
- SLA calculation window: rolling 30-day window for SLA credit calculations. Aggregation for alerting is at 5-minute buckets.

2) Latency measurement:
- p95/p99 are computed over successful generation requests only (2xx). We compute p95/p99 on the server-side elapsed time from request receipt to last token emitted.
- Default measurement window: 7-day rolling for operational dashboards, 30-day rolling for SLA claims.
- Tail handling: we exclude warm-up and known throttling events; exceptions (see below) are documented and subtracted from the SLA denominator if approved.

3) Metrics access and scoping:
- Read-only dashboard: yes. We issue a scoped read-only token tied to the Everleaf account and service keys. This token limits view to your account + environment (prod/stage) and redacts other customers.
- Alerts: we can push to your PagerDuty or Slack; alerts are generated from the same 5-minute aggregated signals and a separate synthetic-health monitor.
- Retention: raw metrics retained for 13 months; 1-minute and 5-minute rollups retained for 13 months.

4) Exception process (planned/unplanned):
- Planned maintenance longer than 2 hours: Redwood must file an exception request at least 72 hours in advance to customer success; customer has an opportunity to accept or request an alternate window.
- Unplanned exceptions (capacity or incident) are triaged; we notify affected customers within 30 minutes of detection with ETA for recovery and a post-incident summary within 72 hours.
- Credits: SLA credits apply per the contract (monthly credit formula attached). Approved exceptions where stringent notice requirements are not met may be eligible for higher credit per contract terms.

Attachments: redwood-slo-measurement-specs.pdf (short spec), dashboard-invite-instructions.txt (how to accept read-only invite).

I'll loop Marcus (infra) and Ben (sales ops) — Marcus can confirm the probe topology and exact aggregation, Ben can confirm contractual credit language.

Best,
Ava Chen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Liu <peter.liu@everleafhealth.com>, ava.chen@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, procurement@everleafhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Procurement] Clarifying SLO measurement and dashboard access (Everleaf)

Thanks Peter — just adding a few infra specifics so your reliability team can vet: 

- Probe topology: global probes run from three public regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) and one private edge in our NV region when customers are in closed networks. Probe requests follow the same auth kube path and exercise model load-balancing.
- Aggregation details: we produce 1-minute and 5-minute aggregates. SLA math uses 5-minute buckets to avoid noisy samples; a 5-minute bucket is considered "down" if >50% of probes in that bucket fail. SLA = 1 - (number_of_down_buckets / total_buckets) over the rolling period.
- Latency sampling: p95/p99 computed per-hour on raw samples then averaged for the rolling window to prevent single-hour spikes from overwhelming long windows.
- Exception handling: when we claim a maintenance exception, we tag the affected buckets in the metric store and expose a boolean "exception_flag" in the read-only view so your team can reproduce SLA math.

If Everleaf wants, we can provide a short reproducible notebook (query → SLA math) against a redacted metric export so you can validate the numbers offline.

On access scoping: we support SCIM/SSO provisioning for team accounts and can issue a short-lived personal token if you prefer.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Inference Infrastructure
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
